notes: 2026-08-03 nightly: TP_R re-derived on real prices, 1.0 -> 3.0 (strategy2.py). This was the last constant still resting on the void Heikin-Ashi numbers, and the audit trail that ran 07-30 measurement, 07-31 justifications, 08-02 ratchet trigger is now closed. THE FINDING: TP_R no longer picks an exit at all. Since 08-02 the ratchet arms at 0.75R, BELOW the take-profit, and cancels it -- so the resting TP only decides where a backstop sits for a dead bot. At 1.0 that backstop sat 0.25R above the arming threshold, making it a truncation device: a move travelling 0.75R -> 1.0R inside one ~20s poll window fills the TP before the ratchet can cancel it, capping the trade at exactly 1R -- and it lands on precisely the fast trending trades the ratchet exists to harvest. NEW TOOL sweep_tp.py, because portfolio2.simulate does not model the take-profit AT ALL (TP_R is invisible to it, which is why it could not just be swept there); sweep_tp reproduces portfolio2 exactly at tp_r=None (asserted in __main__) and adds a resting TP cancelled on arming. Measured worst case (every touch of the TP level fills before the ratchet arms -- a bound, not an estimate, since a 1h bar holds ~180 polls so reality sits near the other end): TP_R 1.0 n=121 WR 57.9% net +15.59% maxDD -9.26% EV +0.129% t=1.32; 2.0 +32.20% t=2.31; 3.0 n=120 WR 56.7% net +39.03% maxDD -9.26% EV +0.325% t=2.61; 5.0 +45.68% t=2.79; no TP n=118 +48.83% t=2.82. 46 of 121 trades (38%) touched 1.0R while unarmed, giving up 36.75R aggregate. Raising the backstop CANNOT turn a winner into a loser: anything reaching 1.0R already armed at 0.75R, so its resting stop is locked at >= +0.75R -- WR barely moves (57.9 -> 56.7) and maxDD does not worsen. Passed every standing rejection test vs 1.0: concurrency cap 1 (+27.5 vs +12.3), cap 2 (+39.0 vs +15.6), cap 4 (+45.1 vs +25.4); alphabetical instead of |stretch| ranking (+34.0 vs +12.8); out-of-sample, where 3.0 is positive in BOTH halves (in-sample +9.94% t=0.94, OOS +29.10% t=2.76) while 1.0 in-sample is NEGATIVE (-2.87%); and independence from last night, holding at the old TRAIL_START_R=1.0 too (+2.41% -> +37.46%). 3.0 not 5.0/none deliberately: the curve is monotonic toward no-TP so the optimum is at the boundary, and picking the boundary of a monotone relationship is a mechanical fact not a measured edge -- same reasoning that kept TRAIL_STEP_R at 0.25. A backstop retains real value against a dead bot; neighbours are smooth (2.0 +32.2%, 3.5 +42.6%, 4.0 +45.7%). ALSO FIXED, a direct consequence of the change: tg.send_signal advertised the TP as the target with an R:R line, so a 3R backstop would have published a goal every trade is DESIGNED to miss. S2 signals now print the real mechanism -- trailing stop arms at +0.75R, floor +15% once armed, backstop TP shown as cancelled-on-arming. S1 rendering byte-unchanged (regression-checked). live.py passes strategy2.TRAIL_START_R through. test_ratchet 10/10 pass. NOT CHANGED: MAX_ADX 25 (07-31 no-EV finding stands, still Mr G call, staged move 25->30), TRAIL_START_R 0.75, TRAIL_STEP_R 0.25, RSI 25/75, stretch 1.5, MAX_TRADES 2, risk 1%, watchlist. CAVEAT recorded honestly: tonight the 5000-bar window rolled and the deployed row moved +33.73% -> +48.83% at unchanged n=118, because the sample edge is concentrated in early-January trades sitting on the window boundary -- the known tail-dependence, unfixed by this change.
